messages:
sara (support): Hey team — raising an escalation from AcmePay. They see normal TTFB on streaming responses but a big p99 tail on total response time (up ~2.1x week over week). Customer says non-stream endpoints are OK. They can reliably repro against our hosted API.

luca (customer): repro steps I used: 
1) curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=rw-large&stream=true" 
2) stream starts almost instantly, first chunk at ~120ms, but final chunk sometimes lands 7–9s later for some requests. p95 looks fine, p99 bad.

sara (support): attaching the request id they sent: req-id=acme-20240228-9f3c. They included a full trace link in their dashboard. They also included a short tcpdump showing lots of tiny chunk writes followed by long idle gaps.

alex (eng-runtime): thanks — initial hypothesis: chunk coalescing/flush-window on the edge proxy changed in last release and might be coalescing tiny writes into larger windows, which can hurt total time for long responses if client stops reading frequently. Can you paste the raw response headers / example trace?

luca (customer): pasted headers for one repro (from curl -i):
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-request-id: acme-20240228-9f3c
via: envoy

and sample chunk timing (relative ms): 120, 240, 250, 255, 256, 7000, 7005. First ~6 chunks <300ms, then a long gap then final flush.

mike (eng-sre): pinging deploy-bot for recent envoy/nginx edge changes. deploy-bot: any config rollouts in the last 36h that affect response buffering / flush_window?

deploy-bot: Recent rollout: envoy-filter v3.2.8 deployed 13:10 UTC (36h ago). Change set: "edge: adaptive coalescing: enable, flush_window_ms default 150". (Change authored by @doris).

alex (eng-runtime): that matches. We previously had flush_window_ms=20 and that gave more frequent small flushes; 150ms will intentionally coalesce to reduce token-level traffic but can create weird long tails if the application emits a small final chunk and then nothing for >flush_window_ms and then final trailer triggers a larger flush later. We need to confirm if the kernel/TCP Nagle interactions and client buffering are amplifying this.

tara (customer-success): AcmePay is on a paid Dedicated trial — they want mitigation now. They asked if we can temporarily disable coalescing for them.

alex (eng-runtime): mitigation options: 
- immediate: route-level override to set flush_window_ms=20 for that customer via our edge config (fast).
- immediate alternative: force non-stream responses for that customer (server-side fallback to buffered endpoint) — easy via routing rule and hides streaming benefits but stabilizes total time.
- medium: tweak adaptive logic to always flush on token boundaries when request is >X tokens or when last emission <Y bytes.
- long-term: add per-customer flush telemetry and auto-adjust heuristics.

mike (eng-sre): I can push a route override to edge for customer acme.com — set flush_window_ms=25. Will need a small env filter patch and a targeted rollout (canary 1% -> 100%). ETA ~45m if no rollbacks.

alex (eng-runtime): please also capture per-request KV cache and kv-ops metrics during canary, and add a trace span to note coalescing decisions. I'll add augmented logging for the next hour.

luca (customer): would prefer non-stream fallback if that is simplest — the app expects whole responses. But happy to test whatever is fastest.

jordan (product): customer experience question — non-stream fallback is a good temporary UX bandaid but we should warn about increased memory/latency on our side. Does route override risk increased cost?

mike (eng-sre): route override to reduce flush window slightly has minimal cost impact. Forcing non-stream could increase memory pressure on heavy requests; I'd avoid if we can tune flush window first.

alex (eng-runtime): to repro locally for devs: curl example (stream):
```
curl -v -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?model=rw-large&stream=true" | ts
```
Also python SSE client:
```
import requests
r = requests.get(url, stream=True)
for chunk in r.iter_content(chunk_size=None):
    print('chunk', len(chunk))
```
If you disable adaptive coalescing on local env/proxy, you see many small writes but final latency goes down for long requests.

alex (eng-runtime): quick log snippet from runtime for req acme-20240228-9f3c: 
```
[2024-02-28T13:02:11.120Z] token_stream: emitted 512 bytes
[2024-02-28T13:02:11.240Z] token_stream: emitted 256 bytes
[2024-02-28T13:02:11.256Z] token_stream: emitted 16 bytes (likely final seq)
[2024-02-28T13:02:11.256Z] flush_decision: coalesce window=150ms -> buffered
[2024-02-28T13:02:18.900Z] proxy: final flush/trailer -> transmitted
```
That 7.6s gap matches customer. Looks like runtime emitted small final payload and edge coalesced it until timer expired or a subsequent event triggered final flush much later.

mike (eng-sre): root cause summary: envoy adaptive coalescing + flush_window_ms bump to 150ms + small final chunk + client behavior = p99 tail. Also possible interaction with Nagle if socket has many tiny writes and kernel waits.

sara (support): recommended immediate action: 
1) mike: roll targeted route override to set flush_window_ms=25 for acme.com (canary 5% for 15m then 100% if good).
2) alex: enable detailed coalescing debug logs for 1 hour for requests with header x-request-id starting with acme-.
3) tara: message customer that we have a mitigation in progress (we can offer non-stream fallback if they prefer while we verify).

mike (eng-sre): creating change now — PR #4867. Pushing canary config. I'll post links to the rollout.

mike (eng-sre): deploy started — canary 5% at 14:05 UTC. Monitoring p95/p99 on the Acme tenant now.

alex (eng-runtime): added a coarse map in runtime to treat last-token <32 bytes as a flush-on-emit (hotfix) for canary requests — lightweight patch that avoids buffering tiny final chunks. Rolling with config gate. PR #4872.

sara (support): Luca — would you like us to flip you to the canary (5%) now so you can confirm improvements?

luca (customer): yes please, flipping now on our side and will run 50 samples.

luca (customer): samples after canary flip: timings: 115, 240, 260, 270, 285, 310 — final flush ~310ms. Looks much better on these 50 samples. p99 seems resolved on our quick check.

mike (eng-sre): metrics look good on the canary — p99 for the tenant dropped from 8.1s -> 320ms. Moving to 100% rollout now.

deploy-bot: Canary completed, promo to 100% started at 14:32 UTC.

mike (eng-sre): promo done. Observability dashboards show steady p99 drop. Rolling back is easy if anything regresses.

jordan (product): good fast fix. Follow-ups: instrument per-tenant coalescing decisions, surface an alert when flush-window-induced p99 delta > 500ms, and consider smarter default for adaptive coalescing (prefer first-byte flush + last-token flush).

alex (eng-runtime): agreed. I'll file a roadmap ticket for auto-tune heuristics and per-tenant overrides. Also want to add an exportable trace field for coalescing decisions.

tara (customer-success): notifying AcmePay: they confirmed improvement and are happy with the fix. I'll close the escalation after we ship the long-term changes.

sara (support): awesome — summary for notes: root cause = edge adaptive coalescing + flush_window_ms increase + small final chunk; immediate mitigation = route-level flush_window reduction + runtime tiny-final-token hotfix; customer verified. Action items: alex -> runtime heuristics ticket; mike -> per-tenant config UI doc; jordan -> product follow-up; tara -> customer confirmation + close. Target: postmortem + long-term plan in 1 week. :thumbsup:

luca (customer): thanks everyone — appreciate the quick turnaround.

sara (support): closing thread when postmortem is linked.
